⏺ Lakes are bodies of fresh or salt water surrounded by land, formed in many ways: glaciers gouging basins, volcanic craters filling with rain, tectonic rifts sinking over time, or rivers pooling
  behind natural dams. Each lake has its own character, shaped by depth, temperature, and the rocks and soils around it. In cold climates they freeze over each winter and thaw each spring. Lakes
  support rich ecosystems, from plankton to fish, turtles, and waterfowl, while aquatic plants filter nutrients and stabilize shorelines. People have long been drawn to them for drinking water, food,
  recreation, and scenery. Yet lakes are deeply sensitive to runoff, pollution, and warming temperatures, which can trigger algal blooms and oxygen loss. Large lakes hold much of the planet's
  accessible fresh water. Whether a small mountain tarn reflecting snowy peaks or a vast inland sea, every lake acts as a mirror of the land and climate around it.
